title: Smart Site map legibility
missionPremise: Operator QA pass on the live surface https://smartsite.cloud, verbatim: 'I cant see street names I think this is important I have to click on a house to see the name of the street'; 'In Zoning C-D-E-F are all orange there is no variance in the colors so how can I tell?'; 'The current flood map is a little hard to read could you color code it... so that we can quickly identify the sections that are in and out of the zones'; 'when I hit find I can not find the property, it will not zoom in or place an arrow on the lot'; 'I am comparing 2 properties and I have no idea where they are, there should be some point of visual reference to show each location'. Command Center is a CONSUMER of Smart Site per operator ruling, so all four fixes land in packages/map-renderer and CC inherits them. Contract read first and built against: _catalog/parcel_fact_sheet_contract/CONTRACT_RULES.md, invariants I4 (failure is not an absence) and I6 (a parcel can be in more than one flood zone at once).
completionPredicate: In satellite mode a stranger can (a) read street names without clicking, (b) tell a C parcel from a D from an E from an F by colour and name each from a legend, (c) tell at a glance which land is inside a FEMA flood zone and which is outside, and (d) see a marker at the resolved subject parcel plus a distinguishable second marker for compare property B. Package builds, both app suites green, Command Center render path unbroken, PR open against main, not merged, not deployed.
scopeBasis: Dispatch file ownership across six parallel lanes in one repo. MINE: packages/map-renderer/src/map/** and src/chrome/satelliteBase.ts. NOT MINE and NOT TOUCHED: chrome/mapToolsController.ts, chrome/MapTools.tsx, chrome/MapToolset.tsx, chrome/LayersControl.tsx (lane P-42); apps/property-explorer/** (lanes P-39/P-40). Files the dispatch left unassigned took MINIMAL ADDITIVE edits only, because a renderer-internal feature cannot reach either app otherwise: src/map-renderer.js, src/FloatingMap.tsx, src/index.ts, src/chrome/index.ts, src/live-gis.ts. Two edits fall outside the four work items entirely and are named as such below (a Command Center test assertion and a CI workflow step). Camera fly and subject state remain lane P-39's; this lane exposes the marker seam and renders, and never moves the camera.

workItems.rootCauseAtSource: packages/map-renderer/src/map/hauska-map-style.js defines ONE raster source (CARTO light_all) whose tiles have street names baked into the image, and chrome/satelliteBase.ts setSatelliteBase() sets that layer's visibility to none whenever satellite is on. Satellite mode therefore had zero street labels by construction.
workItems.fix: New packages/map-renderer/src/map/basemap-labels.js holds the source spec, the layer spec and the measurement that chose them. chrome/satelliteBase.ts mounts it directly ABOVE the Esri imagery and BELOW the first data layer, and binds its visibility to the satellite toggle. Anchored on layerAfter(SATELLITE_LAYER_ID), NOT on firstDataLayerId() — the satellite layer already occupies that slot after the first insert, so re-using it would have put the labels UNDER the imagery.

measurementBehindTheChoice.countingRule: both candidate label tiles and the Esri imagery decoded at 16/15051/27015 (downtown Bastrop), every opaque pixel counted
measurementBehindTheChoice.light_only_labels: glyph #697b89 luminance 120 fully opaque, halo #f6f6f6 luminance 246 at alpha 203-249, glyph-on-halo contrast 4.14:1
measurementBehindTheChoice.dark_only_labels: glyph #6f6f6f luminance 111 fully opaque, halo #232323 luminance 35 at alpha ~204, glyph-on-halo contrast 3.13:1
measurementBehindTheChoice.conclusion: light_only_labels. The white halo separates over the 72.4 percent of imagery below luminance 153 and fails only over the brightest 7.3 percent, and it also carries the higher internal contrast.
measurementBehindTheChoice.endpointProbe: light_only_labels 200 image/png 15,684 bytes; dark_only_labels 200 image/png 15,161 bytes

workItems.offWhenSatelliteOff: Deliberate. With satellite off the CARTO light_all basemap is showing and already carries baked labels; a second labels raster would double-print every street name.

workItems.rootCauseAtSource: gis-map-paint.js landUseFillColorExpr matched a hardcoded ladder of P-5 / P-4 / P-2 / SFR / R-1 / MF / COM / AG and then keyword-scanned landUseDescription. None of those codes occurs in the live browse corpus.
workItems.fix: New packages/map-renderer/src/map/land-use-classes.js: a data-driven classifier on the Texas PTAD state-category letter class read off landUseCode, seven categorical classes plus an 'exempt, utility and other classified' bucket plus a structurally distinct 'not classified here' absence state, with the palette and the legend rows defined next to the rule that paints them.

otherClassified.code: X / G / J / L / M / O / S
otherClassified.label: Exempt, utility and other classified

paletteGates.countingRule: OKLab delta-E x100. CVD is the WORSE of protanopia and deuteranopia under Machado-Oliveira-Fernandes 2009 severity 1.0. ALL-PAIRS list, not adjacent, because a choropleth can put any two classes side by side.
paletteGates.reservedClearance: every slot at least 14 normal-vision delta-E from SUBJECT amber (#f2a23c, #ffe14d, #fff2b0), INTERACTION cyan (#7dd3fc) and the three FEMA fills
paletteGates.excludedHueBands: 52-104 degrees (SUBJECT amber) and 224-276 degrees (INTERACTION cyan plus the FEMA blues), so a land-use fill can never impersonate the subject parcel or the flood layer
paletteGates.chromaFloor: the seven categorical slots are at or above OKLCH chroma 0.10; the two states are deliberately BELOW it so they read as grey rather than as an identity, and sit 17.2 delta-E apart from each other

whySevenAndNotEight.countingRule: max-min search over the legal gamut, worst ALL-PAIRS pair, measured in-session
whySevenAndNotEight.conclusion: Eight classes cannot clear the normal-vision floor of 15 under semantic hue anchoring. Seven can. The exempt family therefore folds into 'other classified' - it is the one common class that is not transactable, which makes it the cheapest fold on a property-research surface. This is a measured ceiling, not a preference.

workItems.secondaryEncoding: The legend (mandatory past three classes in an all-pairs form), the per-class STROKE at full opacity (identity survives a 22 percent fill over imagery), and click-to-inspect naming the class.

workItems.rootCauseAtSource: femaNfhlFillColorExpr matched only FLD_ZONE 'X' and 'X500' to the light step and sent everything else to the mid step, so six real classes in one viewport rendered as three, and effectively two. It also defaulted any unrecognised zone to the 100-year fill, which OVER-CLAIMED hazard.
workItems.fix: New packages/map-renderer/src/map/fema-zones.js: nine classes keyed on FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY and SFHA_TF, with the in/out signal carried by fill-versus-no-fill rather than by a hue difference, and a nine-row legend.

sfhaBfe.label: 1% annual chance, base flood elevation set

minimal.label: Minimal hazard - outside the mapped floodplain

workItems.rampProperties: floodway through shadedX is ONE ordinal ramp: OKLCH hue spread 11 degrees, monotone lightness, every adjacent step at least 0.06 delta-L. It validates as an ordinal ramp against the dark map canvas #16110c AND against a mid-tone satellite surface #787878. openWater and undetermined are deliberately OFF the ramp; undetermined is the only achromatic swatch in the layer.
workItems.howInVersusOutIsCarried: Fill versus no fill. Unshaded Zone X resolves to fill-opacity 0, so land outside the mapped floodplain is drawn EMPTY with only a hairline outline. This buys the contrast the operator asked for without spending any of ROLE_BUDGET.CONTEXT.fillOpacityMax, which exists because of a documented wash-out incident.
honestyFixes: SFHA_TF == 'T' is the honest catch-all, so an SFHA zone code we did not enumerate still renders as IN rather than as unknown.
The match default is now a neutral 'zone not stated' grey. It used to be the 100-year fill.
In/out is THREE states, never two: null means FEMA published no determination, which is not the same as 'outside'.
I6 multiplicity is stated on the legend: 'A parcel can sit in more than one zone at once.'

workItems.rootCauseAtSource: Nothing drew a marker anywhere in the renderer. The subject parcel does get a feature-state amber glow via parcel-tiles.js, but only once its vector tile has painted, it is invisible at low zoom, and it cannot mark a comparison property at all.

theSeamForP39.reExportedOn: FloatingMapHandle.setSubjectMarkers (plus getSubjectMarkers), and from the package barrel as the SubjectMarker type
theSeamForP39.signature: setSubjectMarkers(markers: Array<{ id?: string|number; longitude?: number; latitude?: number; lng?: number; lat?: number; role?: 'primary'|'secondary'; label?: string }>): void
contract: The argument is the COMPLETE marker set. Passing [] or omitting it clears every marker.
Safe to call before the style loads - the set is stashed and replayed on the map `load` event, the same way overlays are.
Entries without finite coordinates are DROPPED rather than drawn at 0,0.
role defaults to 'primary'; label defaults to 'A' for primary and 'B' for secondary; an explicit label always wins.
This lane NEVER moves the camera and never reads parcel feature-state. P-39 owns the fly and the subject state and calls this with resolved coordinates.
theSeamForP39.zOrder: raiseSubjectMarkers() re-lifts the four layers after applyOverlays and applyLayerVisibility, because reconcileOverlays and reorderGisLayers both call moveLayer and would otherwise bury the SUBJECT role.

workItems.aVersusB: Property A is a solid amber bullseye; property B is a hollow ring (zero-radius core, thicker ring stroke). SHAPE carries the distinction, not hue, so the pair survives the glyph endpoint being unavailable and so the taxonomy's reserved SUBJECT amber is not duplicated into a second reserved colour. text-font is ['Noto Sans Medium'], probed 200 at the configured protomaps endpoint on 2026-08-18 ('Open Sans Regular' and 'Noto Sans Bold' both return 404 there, so a wrong stack would have drawn nothing silently).

outsideTheFourWorkItems.why: an assertion required the FEMA opacity expression to contain the literal 'X500'. FEMA does not publish that FLD_ZONE value - the 500-year band is FLD_ZONE 'X' with ZONE_SUBTY '0.2 PCT ANNUAL CHANCE FLOOD HAZARD' (86 of 204 features in the live probe). The old paint matched a zone code that does not exist and the test locked it in. Re-pointed at the real fields, plus a second CC test asserting minimal-hazard land paints at opacity 0. correctionsToTheDispatch.dispatchClaim: Real Texas district codes (C, D, E, F, GC, SF-1, MU) match nothing and all fall through to C.other.fill. They are orange because they are all classed unclassified, not because anyone chose orange four times.
correctionsToTheDispatch.quotedSource: packages/map-renderer/src/map/gis-map-paint.js at 5bf06ec, landUseFillColorExpr: after the eight `["==", code, ...]` branches the expression continues with `["!=", ["index-of", "commercial", desc], -1], C.commercial.fill` and fifteen further description keyword branches before reaching `C.other.fill`.
correctionsToTheDispatch.correction: The CODE ladder does miss everything, but a DESCRIPTION keyword ladder underneath it catches roughly 74 percent of a real Bastrop tile. Measured on z16/15051/27015: F1 (81 features) hits 'commercial'; A1/A2/A3 (58) hit 'single'; B2 (6) hits 'multi'; E2 (1) hits 'farm'. Only 53 of 203 features (26.1 percent) actually reach C.other.fill.
correctionsToTheDispatch.whyItStillMatters: The surviving defects are arguably worse than the one described. C1 vacant lands on #c98f5e and F1 commercial on #ff8c1a - two oranges 9.7 delta-E apart, which is literally 'C-D-E-F are all orange'. E1 rural paints IDENTICALLY to A1 single-family because 'Rural single-family residential (farm/ranch improvement)' also contains 'single'. And XV exempt (a positive determination, 40 features) paints IDENTICALLY to the 5 features with no code at all, which is DEV_PROCESS 4.3 violated in paint. The remedy is unchanged.

correctionsToTheDispatch.dispatchClaim: Real Texas district codes (C, D, E, F, GC, SF-1, MU)
correctionsToTheDispatch.correction: GC, SF-1 and MU are municipal zoning district codes. The browse corpus does not carry municipal zoning at all; the PMTiles vector layer's only land-use field is `landUseCode`, which carries county CAD state-category codes. Verified from the archive's own tilestats and from decoded tiles.
correctionsToTheDispatch.consequence: The LAYERS row is labelled 'Zoning / land use' but paints assessor classification. Logged as backlog item W3-B2 for an operator ruling on the label.

correctionsToTheDispatch.dispatchClaim: Only AE and X_500 currently have distinct subcodes in GIS_LAYER_PAINT.
correctionsToTheDispatch.correction: True of the FIXTURE table in hauska-map-style.js, but that table is not what Smart Site renders. The live FEMA overlay is painted by femaNfhlFillColorExpr in layer-role-taxonomy.js, whose match keys 'X' and 'X500'. 'X500' is not a value FEMA publishes; the real 500-year band is FLD_ZONE 'X' with ZONE_SUBTY '0.2 PCT ANNUAL CHANCE FLOOD HAZARD'. So the live surface matched a zone code that does not exist, and a Command Center test asserted on that same non-existent code.

backlogFindings.finding: the `meshMode && layerKey === 'parcel-polygon'` branch computes `fillOpacityExpr(layerKey, true) * saturation` with no type guard. That call returns a MapLibre `case` ARRAY for parcel-polygon, so the multiply yields NaN and setPaintProperty receives NaN. The two neighbouring branches DO guard with `typeof baseOpacity === 'number'`.
